title: Popularity-Aware Alignment and Contrast for Mitigating Popularity Bias

problem.claim: Collaborative filtering suffers from popularity bias, creating an accuracy gap between popular and unpopular items and hindering accurate preference understanding.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not adequately extract common supervision from popular items for unpopular-item representations or alleviate popularity-induced representation separation.

contributions.claim: PAAC models common supervisory signals in popular-item representations and uses a popularity-aware supervised alignment module to learn unpopular-item representations.
PAAC re-weights the contrastive learning loss from a popularity-centric perspective to mitigate representation separation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present PAAC and its popularity-aware supervised alignment module as novel contributions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validating PAAC's effectiveness and rationale through extensive experiments on three real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Popularity bias in collaborative filtering creates unequal performance across popular and unpopular items.
Prior efforts leave unresolved the transfer of supervision from popular items and popularity-related representation separation.
PAAC addresses the two challenges with popularity-aware supervised alignment and re-weighted contrastive learning.
The authors evaluate PAAC on three real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The method transfers common supervisory signals from popular-item representations to improve representations of unpopular items.

interpretation.claim: Information-rich or frequently observed groups may provide supervision for improving underrepresented groups.

application.claim: In other imbalanced representation-learning settings, consider supervised alignment from well-observed groups alongside imbalance-aware contrastive weighting.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the approach transfers beyond popularity bias or the evaluated datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, loss formulation, or re-weighting scheme in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or sensitivity analyses.
